title: Deficiency Balance Accounts: Monthly Installment of an Installment Settlement
content:
**The settlement amount.** The settlement amount of an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts is the offer amount of the account's installment settlement offer with the status accepted, the largest such amount where the account carries more than one, and the settlement is started under the offer that amount comes from.

**The installment.** An installment settlement is spread over a standard number of installments equal to the band's maximum number of settlement installments, and each monthly installment is the settlement amount divided by that number, rounded up to the cent.

**Order of the figures.** A schedule that replaces the standard number of installments is applied first; the installment cuts of the schedules that apply are then subtracted from that number and the installment additions added to it; the number is then held to at least one and at most the band's maximum number of settlement installments, and the settlement amount is divided by it and rounded up to the cent.

## Band figures used

| Band 1 | Band 2 | Band 3 | Band 4 | Band 5 | Band 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 3 | 4 | 6 | 6 | 6 |

(maximum number of settlement installments)

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

| Band | Settlement amount | Number of installments | Monthly installment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Band 1 | $900.00 | 3 | $300.00 |
| Band 4 | $5,600.00 | 6 | $933.34 ($933.333... rounded up) |
| Band 3 | $2,000.00 | 4 | $500.00 |

A hypothetical illustration of the order: Band 4, settlement amount $5,600.00, one installment cut and no addition. The number is 6 less 1, that is 5, within one and six; $5,600.00 divided by 5 is $1,120.00. With cuts totalling 7 the number would be held at one, and with additions taking it above six it would be held at six.

When two accepted installment settlement offers of $3,000.00 and $3,200.00 are on the account, the settlement amount is $3,200.00, and the settlement is started under that offer.
